outcomes: recognize the main parts of a laptop or desktop computer and the everyday words for them
control your computer with the mouse, keyboard and windows, including right-clicking and switching between programs
create, name, find, copy, move and organize files and folders
download and upload files, open ZIP files, and know where your files are stored
use a web browser with tabs, web addresses and bookmarks
take a screenshot and use the most common keyboard shortcuts
work through a computer problem calmly, step by step, instead of panicking
keep your computer and accounts safe with simple everyday habits

fit_check.text: I can turn a computer on, sign in, and restart or shut it down properly.
I can right-click, drag an item, and switch between open windows.
I can take a screenshot and find where it was saved.
I can create a folder, rename a file, and explain the difference between copying and moving a file.
I can find a file I just downloaded and open a ZIP file.
I can open a new tab, go to a web address, and bookmark a page.
When something on my computer stops working, I know what to check and try before asking for help.
I can recognize a suspicious link or attachment and I know how to keep my accounts safe.

lessons.title: Meet Your Computer
next_preview: Now that you know the parts of your computer, it's time to control it.
Next, you'll practice the mouse and keyboard actions you'll use hundreds of times a day, including right-clicking, switching between windows, and taking a screenshot.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check that the main words from this lesson are clear.

questions.q: Which of these is an operating system?
questions.explain: Windows and macOS are operating systems: the main system that runs the whole computer. Chrome is an application that runs on top of it.

questions.q: You're going to be away from your laptop for three minutes to get water. What is the most sensible thing to do?
options: Leave everything open as it is
questions.explain: Locking keeps your work open but hides it until you sign in again. Shutting down for a short break is unnecessary, and leaving the screen open lets anyone see your work.

questions.q: Where do you usually find the programs that are currently open on a Windows computer?
options: On the taskbar at the bottom of the screen
questions.explain: The taskbar (the Dock on a Mac) shows your open programs, so you can switch between them.

lessons.title: Mouse, Keyboard & Windows
next_preview: You can now control your computer. Next, you'll learn to handle the thing almost every VA task involves: files.
Lesson 3 covers creating folders, copying and moving, naming files clearly, and finding a file when you can't remember where it went.

l2.title: Which Action Helps?
l2.intro: Choose the action that solves each situation fastest.

items.q: You want to rename a file on your desktop, but you can't see a Rename button anywhere.
items.good: Right-clicking a file shows the actions available for it, including Rename.
items.try: Right-click the file. The menu that appears includes Rename and other file actions.

items.q: You're copying product details from a website into a spreadsheet, and keep losing your place when you switch between them.
options: Put the two windows side by side
Take a screenshot of the spreadsheet
items.good: Side by side, you can read one window while typing in the other.
items.try: Put the two windows side by side, so you can read one while typing in the other.

items.q: You need to find the word "refund" in a 40-page document.
items.good: Find jumps straight to every place the word appears.
items.try: Use Find (Ctrl/⌘ + F). It jumps straight to every place the word appears.

items.q: You accidentally deleted a paragraph you still needed.
items.good: Undo reverses your last action right away.
items.try: Undo (Ctrl/⌘ + Z) reverses your last action right away. Saving would keep the mistake.

items.q: A website shows an error message and you want to show it to someone who can help.
options: Take a screenshot of the error
Close the page and try to forget it
Copy the whole page's address only
items.good: A screenshot shows exactly what you saw, including the exact error wording.
items.try: Take a screenshot. It shows exactly what you saw, including the exact wording of the error.

items.q: You took an area screenshot on a Mac with <kbd>⌘</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>4</kbd>. Where do you look for it first?
items.good: Mac screenshots are saved to the Desktop by default.
items.try: Look on the Desktop. That's where a Mac saves screenshots by default.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the everyday controls from this lesson.

questions.q: What's the difference between minimizing and closing a window?
options: Minimizing hides it but keeps it open; closing closes it
Closing hides it on the taskbar
questions.explain: A minimized window waits on the taskbar or Dock. A closed window is gone until you open it again, so save before closing.

questions.q: On a Mac, which key does most of the work that Ctrl does on Windows in shortcuts?
questions.explain: Ctrl + C on Windows is ⌘ + C on a Mac, and the same pattern works for most everyday shortcuts.

questions.q: You're about to send a client a screenshot. What should you check first?
options: That it shows nothing private, like passwords or another client's information
That it is in black and white
That it is the whole screen
Nothing, screenshots are always fine to send
questions.explain: A screenshot shows everything in the captured area. Check for passwords, private messages and other clients' details before sending.

lessons.title: Files & Folders
next_preview: Your files are organized. Next: how files get onto your computer and back off it.
Lesson 4 covers device and cloud storage, downloading, ZIP files and uploading.

l3.title: What Would You Do?
l3.intro: Everyday file situations. Choose the best action.

items.q: A client sends 20 product photos. You need to crop them, but the client wants the originals kept exactly as they are.
options: Move the photos into your working folder
Copy the photos into your working folder and crop the copies
items.good: Copying keeps the originals untouched while you work on duplicates.
items.try: Copy them. Copying keeps the originals untouched while you work on the duplicates.

items.q: Which is the clearest name for a September invoice for a client named Rivera?
items.good: It says what the file is, who it's for, and when, and it will sort by date.
items.try: invoice-rivera-2026-09.pdf says what it is, who it's for and when, so anyone can find it.

items.q: You saved a file an hour ago but can't remember which folder. What's a good first step?
options: Search for part of the file name in File Explorer or Finder
Make the file again from scratch
Empty the Recycle Bin or Trash
items.good: Searching for part of the name is usually the fastest way to find it.
items.try: Search for part of the file name first. Emptying the Recycle Bin or Trash could destroy the file if it was deleted by mistake.

items.q: You deleted a file by mistake a few minutes ago. Where can you get it back?
options: From the Recycle Bin (Windows) or Trash (Mac)
items.good: Deleted files stay in the Recycle Bin or Trash until it's emptied, and you can restore them.
items.try: Check the Recycle Bin (Windows) or Trash (Mac). You can restore the file from there until it's emptied.

items.q: You're editing a price list and want to keep the old version as well as the new one.
options: Save As, with a new name
items.good: Save As makes a new file with your changes and leaves the original as it was.
items.try: Use Save As with a new name. Save would replace the old version.

items.q: A client sends orders.csv. What kind of file is it?
items.good: .csv is plain spreadsheet data, often exported from another system.
items.try: .csv is plain spreadsheet data, often exported from a store or another system.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the file skills from this lesson.

questions.q: You drag a file from Folder A into Folder B on the same drive. What usually happens?
options: It moves: it's now only in Folder B
It copies: it's in both folders
It turns into a ZIP file
questions.explain: Dragging within the same drive moves the file. Use Copy and Paste when the original must stay where it is.

questions.q: Why write dates in file names as year-month-day, like 2026-09-15?
options: So files sort in the right date order
Because computers can't read other formats
questions.explain: Year-month-day names sort in date order automatically, which makes the newest version easy to spot.

questions.q: When you rename a file, which part should you leave unchanged?
options: Nothing needs to stay the same
questions.explain: Changing the extension can make the computer open the file with the wrong program, or not open it at all.

lessons.title: Storage, Downloads & Uploads
next_preview: Most files you download come from the internet, through a web browser. Next, you'll learn how the browser itself works.
Lesson 5 covers web addresses, tabs, bookmarks and the other browser basics you'll use every day.

l4.title: Follow the File
l4.intro: A client emails you a ZIP file of product photos. Choose the right step at each point.

items.q: You download the ZIP file. Where does it most likely go?
options: Straight into the client's cloud folder
items.good: Downloads go to the Downloads folder unless you chose a different place.
items.try: It most likely goes to Downloads, unless you chose a different place when downloading.

items.q: You open the ZIP and see the photos. What should you do before working on them?
options: Edit them directly inside the ZIP
Extract the ZIP, then work from the extracted folder
Upload the ZIP back to the client
items.good: Extracting gives you a normal folder of files you can open, edit and save properly.
items.try: Extract it first. Files opened from inside a ZIP often can't be saved properly.

items.q: After extracting, the photos are sitting in Downloads. What's the best next step?
options: Move the extracted folder into the right work folder
Delete the ZIP and the photos
Copy them to the Desktop too
items.good: Moving the folder into its proper place keeps your work organized and easy to find.
items.try: Move the extracted folder into the right work folder so it's organized and easy to find.

items.q: You try to download another file, but the computer says there isn't enough space. What should you check?
options: Your storage, and clear out your own old downloads and large files
Delete the client's files to make room
items.good: Check your storage and remove your own unneeded files, like old downloads and a full Recycle Bin or Trash.
items.try: Check your storage settings and clear your own old downloads and large files. Never delete a client's files to make room.

items.q: You finish the photos and upload them to the client's folder online. What should you do before closing the tab?
options: Wait for the upload to finish and check the files appear with the right names
Delete the photos from your computer
items.good: Closing the tab early can stop the upload. Checking confirms the files really arrived.
items.try: Wait for the upload to finish, then check the files are really there, with the right names.

items.q: True or false: uploading a file to a cloud folder automatically lets other people see it.
items.good: Uploading only puts a copy online. Who can see it depends on the folder's sharing settings, which the next course covers.
items.try: False. Uploading only puts a copy online. Who can see it depends on sharing settings, covered in the next course.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the difference between storage, downloading and uploading.

questions.q: Which describes downloading?
options: Copying a file from the internet to your computer
Copying a file from your computer to the internet
questions.explain: Download: internet → your computer. Upload is the opposite direction.

questions.q: What is one advantage of cloud storage over device storage?
options: You can reach the files from any device where you sign in
It works without internet on every device
questions.explain: Cloud files are available wherever you sign in, and they're safe if your computer breaks. Device files work offline, but only on that computer.

questions.q: You downloaded the same file twice. Which one is probably the newer copy?
options: The one with (1) added to the name
Both are identical, so it never matters
The one with the older date
questions.explain: The second download usually gets a number such as (1) added. Check the date if you're unsure which is newest.

lessons.title: Browser Basics
next_preview: You now know the everyday tools. Next: what to do when one of them stops working.
Lesson 6 gives you a step-by-step way to work through computer problems calmly, and to ask for help in a way that gets you answers fast.

l5.title: In the Browser
l5.intro: Choose the best action for each situation.

items.q: A client tells you to go to www.meadowlanehome.com/admin. What's the best way to get there?
options: Type the address into the address bar and press Enter
Search Google for "meadow lane home" and click the first result
Ask the client to send a screenshot of the page
Open a Private window and search for it
items.good: With an exact address, go straight there. Search results can lead to the wrong, or a fake, site.
items.try: Type the exact address into the address bar. Searching can lead you to the wrong site, or a fake one.

items.q: You closed a tab by accident and need it back.
options: Search for it again from scratch
items.good: Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + T reopens the tab you just closed.
items.try: Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + T reopens the tab you just closed. Ctrl/⌘ + W would close another one.

items.q: A page shows yesterday's numbers, but you know they changed this morning.
items.good: Refresh loads the page again with the latest information.
items.try: Refresh the page. It loads the page again with the latest information.

items.q: You'll use a client's order dashboard every day.
items.good: A bookmark opens the exact page in one click.
items.try: Bookmark it (Ctrl/⌘ + D) so the exact page is one click away.

items.q: You want to open a link from a report without losing your place in the report.
options: Right-click the link and choose Open link in new tab
Copy the report into a document first
items.good: A new tab keeps your report open in the original tab.
items.try: Right-click the link and choose Open link in new tab, so the report stays open.

items.q: What does a Private or Incognito window do?
options: Doesn't keep your history or stay signed in after you close it
Hides everything you do from every website
items.good: It forgets your history and sign-ins when closed, which is useful on shared computers. Websites can still see what you do.
items.try: It only forgets your history and sign-ins when you close it. It doesn't hide you from websites or protect against viruses.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the browser basics from this lesson.

questions.q: Which of these is a web browser?
questions.explain: Edge, Chrome, Safari and Firefox are browsers. Google search is a search engine you visit inside a browser.

questions.q: Where do you see the web address of the page you're on?
options: In the address bar at the top of the browser
questions.explain: The address bar shows the current page's address, and it's where you type an address to go somewhere.

questions.q: You have 35 tabs open and the computer is getting slow. What's a sensible habit?
options: Close tabs you've finished with and bookmark ones you'll need again
Open a new window for each tab
questions.explain: Every open tab uses memory. Closing finished tabs and bookmarking the rest keeps the computer fast and your work easy to find.

lessons.title: Basic Troubleshooting
next_preview: Some problems are more serious than a page that won't load: fake messages, stolen passwords, harmful downloads.
Lesson 7 covers the everyday habits that keep your computer, your accounts and your clients' information safe.

l6.title: What's the Next Step?
l6.intro: Work through each problem with STOP → CHECK → TRY → SEARCH → ASK.

items.q: You click Save and an error message pops up. What do you do first?
options: Read the whole message and take a screenshot
Message the client that the computer is broken
Click every button on the message
items.good: STOP: read the exact message and capture it before anything else changes.
items.try: STOP first: read the whole message and take a screenshot. Closing the program could lose your work.

items.q: No websites will load, not just one. What should you CHECK?
items.good: If every site fails, the internet connection is the most likely cause.
items.try: When every site fails, check your internet connection first.

items.q: A client's online tool shows "Access denied" when you open a link they sent.
options: Check which account you're signed in to
items.good: Being signed in to the wrong account is one of the most common causes of access errors.
items.try: Check which account you're signed in to. A wrong account is one of the most common causes of access errors.

items.q: The internet is fine but one page still looks broken. What's a simple thing to TRY?
options: Refresh the page, or try another browser
items.good: Refreshing or trying another browser are quick, safe fixes that often work.
items.try: Try a quick, safe fix first: refresh the page or open it in another browser.

items.q: You tried the simple fixes and have the exact error text. Which search is most useful?
options: The exact error text plus the program's name
items.good: The exact error plus the program's name leads to people who had the same problem.
items.try: Search the exact error text with the program's name. That's how you find people who had the same problem.

items.q: You still can't fix it. Which help request is best?
options: What happened, what you were doing, what you tried, and the exact error
A long message about how stressful your day has been
items.good: Those four details let someone help you quickly, without a round of questions.
items.try: Include what happened, what you were doing, what you tried, and the exact error. That lets someone help you quickly.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the troubleshooting steps from this lesson.

questions.q: What's the correct order?
questions.explain: Stop and look, check the obvious causes, try safe fixes, search the exact problem, then ask with the details.

questions.q: A forum post says to fix your problem by downloading a small program from an unknown website. What should you do?
options: Stop and ask someone you trust before doing it
Download it on the client's computer instead
questions.explain: Risky fixes can cause bigger problems than the original one. When a fix feels risky, stop and ask.

questions.q: A program is completely frozen on Windows. Which shortcut opens Task Manager so you can close it?
questions.explain: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager on Windows. On a Mac, ⌘ + Option + Esc opens Force Quit.

lessons.title: Security & Safe Computer Habits
next_preview: You've now covered every skill in this course. The last lesson puts them together.
Lesson 8 walks through one complete computer task from start to finish, using what you learned in Lessons 1 to 7.

l7.title: What Would You Do?
l7.intro: Realistic situations. Use judgment, not fear.

items.q: An email that looks like it's from your client's bank says their account will be locked today unless you sign in using the link.
options: Click the link and sign in quickly
Don't click. Go to the bank's website yourself, or check with the client
Forward it to all your contacts
items.good: Urgency plus a sign-in link is a classic phishing sign. Go to the real site yourself or check with the client.
items.try: Don't click. Urgency plus a sign-in link is a classic phishing sign. Open the real site yourself or check with the client.

items.q: A client asks for the password to a shared account. How should you send it?
options: Through the password manager or method the client uses for sharing access
items.good: Passwords shouldn't sit in chats or emails. Use the secure method the client uses.
items.try: Use the password manager or secure method the client uses. Chats and emails keep passwords where others can find them.

items.q: Someone calls saying they're from a software company and asks for the code that was just sent to your phone.
options: Don't share it, and end the call
items.good: Sign-in codes are only for you. Real companies don't ask for them.
items.try: Never share it. Sign-in codes are only for you, and real companies don't ask for them.

items.q: You finish a task on a computer at an internet café.
options: Sign out of every account, then close the private window
Save your password so it's faster next time
Leave it on for the next person
items.good: Signing out fully means the next person can't get into your accounts.
items.try: Sign out of every account before you leave. Closing the browser alone may leave you signed in.

items.q: Your laptop has shown an update notice for a week.
options: Save your work and install the update at a sensible time
items.good: Updates often fix security problems. Save your work and install them promptly.
items.try: Save your work and install it at a sensible time. Many updates fix security problems.

items.q: You realize you typed a client's account password into a page that now looks fake.
options: Say nothing and hope it's fine
Change the password on the real site right away and tell the client
Wait a week to see if anything happens
items.good: Acting fast and telling the client limits the damage.
items.try: Change the password on the real site right away and tell the client. Acting fast is what limits the damage.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the safety habits from this lesson.

questions.q: Why is using the same password for several accounts risky?
options: If one site is hacked, the same password opens your other accounts
It makes the password too long
questions.explain: A reused password turns one hacked website into access to all your other accounts. Use a password manager to keep them different.

questions.q: How can you see where a link really goes before clicking it?
options: Hold the pointer over it and read the address that appears
Right-click and choose Copy, then paste it into the address bar and press Enter
questions.explain: Hovering shows the real destination, usually at the bottom of the window, without opening it.

questions.q: Which shortcut locks a Windows computer?
questions.explain: ⊞ Win + L locks Windows. On a Mac, use Control + ⌘ + Q.

lessons.title: Putting It Together: A Basic Computer Workflow
next_preview: You've finished every lesson. The Final Challenge is 12 short scenario questions covering the whole course.
It's diagnostic, not a test you pass or fail: your score shows what's solid and which lessons are worth another look.

l8.title: When a Step Goes Wrong
l8.intro: Things rarely go perfectly. Choose the best response.

items.q: You double-click the ZIP and can see the photos, but the Rename option doesn't work on them.
options: Extract the ZIP first, then rename the extracted photos
Ask the client to send the photos one by one
items.good: Files inside a ZIP often can't be changed. Extract first, then work on the extracted copies.
items.try: Extract the ZIP first. Files viewed inside a ZIP often can't be renamed or saved.

items.q: The download finished, but the ZIP isn't on your Desktop.
options: Download it again five more times
Check the Downloads folder or the browser's download list
Tell the client the link is broken
items.good: Downloads go to the Downloads folder by default, and the browser's download list can open it directly.
items.try: Check Downloads, or open the browser's download list. That's where downloads go by default.

items.q: The upload has been stuck at the same point for ten minutes.
options: Close the tab and assume it worked
STOP and CHECK: is your internet working? If the upload failed, try it again
Delete the photos from your computer
Upload a screenshot of the photos instead
items.good: Check the connection first, and never assume a stuck upload finished.
items.try: Use STOP → CHECK: confirm your internet is working, and retry the upload if it failed. Never assume a stuck upload finished.

items.q: Your screenshot of the folder also shows another client's email in a second window.
options: Send it anyway, it's only a screenshot
Take a new screenshot of just the folder
Send it but ask them not to look
items.good: Screenshots should show only what's needed. Capture just the folder.
items.try: Take a new screenshot of just the folder. Another client's information should never appear in work you send.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check that you can connect the course skills into one workflow.

questions.q: Why should you extract a ZIP before renaming the files inside it?
options: Files inside a ZIP often can't be changed or saved properly
Renaming inside a ZIP deletes the files
ZIP files can't be opened on a Mac
questions.explain: Extracting gives you normal files you can rename, edit and save.

questions.q: When should you take the screenshot of the renamed files?
questions.explain: The screenshot is proof of the finished names, so take it once the renaming is done.

questions.q: The upload says it's complete. What's left to do?
options: Check that all the files appear on the page with the right names
Upload them again to be safe
questions.explain: Checking confirms the work actually arrived as expected, so nobody finds a problem later.
